data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's variance-reduction mechanism presupposes independent binary verifications and invokes the Law of Large Numbers to cancel idiosyncratic noise, but its countercondition admits tasks where variables cannot be decomposed without losing emergent information. On exactly those tasks the 'independent sub-claims' assumption fails: non-expert errors on the sub-claims become correlated because they all miss the same interaction, so aggregation no longer cancels noise and can amplify a shared blind spot. SRC_002 gives no within-evaluation evidence that would reveal this correlated-error breakdown versus a genuine reliability gain, so it leaves the problem's distinguishing-evidence requirement unmet.
